algorithm.Title: Hair Loss - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Hair loss assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.

Background.ExpertReviewer: PENDING: Qatar adolescent/adult, obstetric, dermatology, mental-health, safeguarding, and nursing governance review

FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Follow the relevant exposure, burn, anaphylaxis, poisoning, severe-illness, suicide-safety, or safeguarding instructions from 999. Do not apply chemicals, attempt decontamination beyond emergency instructions, or give unprescribed medicine. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is an inflamed, painful, scaling, crusting, or infected-looking scalp the main concern rather than hair loss itself?
questions.Information: The localized-rash family is not generated. Arrange prompt in-person assessment through the Qatar route approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED).

questions.Question: Is hair/scalp change part of a current emergency: chemical or electrical exposure, major burn, facial/airway swelling, breathing difficulty, collapse, severe infection with confusion, poisoning/overdose, severe dehydration/malnutrition, or immediate self-harm/safeguarding danger?
questions.Information: Hair loss alone is generally not an emergency, but the reported presentation may be secondary to a time-critical exposure, allergic reaction, infection, poisoning, malnutrition, mental-health crisis, or safeguarding threat.

questions.Question: Is the caller worried about the hair loss and would like it assessed?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance: arrange clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) if you're worried about your hair loss, to identify the cause before considering commercial hair clinic options.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency response for the underlying danger
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Follow the relevant exposure, burn, anaphylaxis, poisoning, severe-illness, suicide-safety, or safeguarding instructions from 999. Do not apply chemicals, attempt decontamination beyond emergency instructions, or give unprescribed medicine. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: airway or breathing change; collapse, confusion, or severe illness; chemical/burn exposure; self-harm or safeguarding danger.

advice.Title: Governed in-person hair-loss assessment
Content: Arrange an in-person assessment through the Qatar route and timing approved by governance to evaluate pattern, scalp disease, medicines, nutrition, endocrine illness, pregnancy/postpartum factors, traction/pulling, and psychosocial impact. Do not start supplements, topical medicines, or hair-loss drugs without age, pregnancy, diagnosis, interaction, and laboratory review. For an adolescent, provide private age-appropriate assessment with approved caregiver and safeguarding practice.
Call Back If: rapid or patchy progression; scalp pain, inflammation, pus, or scarring; weight loss, restrictive eating, systemic illness, or severe distress.

references: NHS.UK, "Hair loss", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hair-loss/ (page last reviewed 24 January 2024)

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant/recently postpartum, and when/how quickly did hair loss begin? This protocol starts at age 12; younger children require an approved pediatric route.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is it patchy, all over, or a receding pattern?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 4 runtime protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is there scalp pain, redness, swelling, pus, blistering, chemical/thermal exposure, new medicine, fever, weight loss, restrictive eating, endocrine symptoms, pregnancy/postpartum change, hair pulling/traction, distress/self-harm concern, or a safeguarding concern?
